evals.name: dim-layer-behind-modal
evals.prompt: What's the UI term for the dark see-through layer that covers the page behind a centered popup? You can still see the page, but you can't click it until the popup closes. I need the right phrase for a coding-agent prompt and a couple of real component references.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the layer as a scrim or backdrop (with modal overlay as a less precise alias), distinguishes it from the dialog itself, gives prompt-ready wording, and links directly to authoritative modal or overlay guidance.

assertions.text: Names scrim or backdrop as the top match and explains that the layer is separate from the modal dialog.
Returns direct authoritative example links and no link from namethatui.com or a subdomain.
Includes concise prompt-ready wording that mentions both the dialog and its dimmed background layer.

evals.name: editable-suggestions-field
evals.prompt: I mean that search-ish form control where I type 'au', a list opens under the field, the options narrow to Australia and Austria, and choosing one fills the field. What is that component actually called? Give me the closest names and links so I can brief an engineer.
evals.expected_output: Ranks editable combobox first, treats autocomplete/typeahead as common product-language aliases, distinguishes it from select, listbox, and command menu behavior, and links to WAI-ARIA or MDN guidance.

assertions.text: Ranks combobox as the semantic pattern and includes autocomplete or typeahead as an alias.
Uses value selection and typing/filtering to distinguish the result from a menu or plain select.
Provides at least one direct W3C or MDN component link.

evals.name: three-dot-secondary-actions
evals.prompt: On each row there's a vertical three-dot button. Pressing it opens Rename, Duplicate, Archive, and Delete for that row. I keep calling it a kebab but I suspect that's only the icon. What should I call the whole UI control, and what are plausible alternatives?
evals.expected_output: Identifies an overflow or more-actions menu implemented as a menu button, explains that kebab names the icon rather than the interaction, and gives direct examples.

assertions.text: Names overflow menu or more-actions menu as the user-facing pattern.
Explains that kebab refers to the icon orientation, while menu button describes the interaction semantics.
Returns one to three ranked matches with direct links.

evals.name: visual-modal-and-scrim
evals.prompt: Look at the attached UI screenshot. Name the floating component and the dark layer behind it. Explain what you can observe versus what the still image cannot prove, then give me prompt-ready wording and authoritative examples.
evals.expected_output: Uses local image analysis, identifies a centered dialog/modal and a scrim/backdrop, separates visible evidence from unknown focus/modality behavior, and returns direct authoritative links without uploading the fixture.

assertions.text: Identifies both the centered dialog/modal and the scrim/backdrop as separate UI parts.
Separates visible observations from focus, keyboard, and modality behavior that a screenshot cannot prove.
Does not upload or send the image to a third-party vision service.
Includes prompt-ready wording and at least one direct authoritative example link.

evals.name: visual-tree-disclosure
evals.prompt: The attached screenshot is from a desktop file navigator. What is the small rotating triangle beside a folder row called, and what is the larger parent pattern? Give me the common name, any platform term you can support, and useful links.
evals.expected_output: Identifies a disclosure triangle/disclosure control inside a tree or outline view, avoids mislabeling the whole control as an accordion, and supports platform-specific terms only with direct evidence.

assertions.text: Names disclosure triangle or disclosure control as the small control.
Names tree view or outline view as the parent pattern and explains why accordion is weaker.
Attributes any native class or platform term to a direct primary source rather than inferring it from appearance.

evals.name: dom-aria-combobox-clues
evals.prompt: Can you name this pattern from the DOM? The input has role='combobox', aria-autocomplete='list', aria-expanded='true', and aria-controls='city-results'. The controlled element has role='listbox'; its rows have role='option'. Typing filters the rows and Enter copies the active option into the input. Explain the likely component and whether the attributes alone are enough proof.
evals.expected_output: Identifies an editable autocomplete combobox, explains how the behavior corroborates the roles, warns that ARIA labels alone can be wrong, distinguishes listbox as the popup primitive, and links to primary guidance.

assertions.text: Identifies an editable autocomplete combobox and the associated listbox popup.
States that ARIA roles are evidence rather than proof and reconciles them with the described behavior.
Links directly to WAI-ARIA APG or MDN guidance.

evals.name: mobile-bottom-surface
evals.prompt: On mobile, tapping Share dims the screen and slides a rounded panel up from the bottom. It has a drag handle, a row of share targets, Copy link, and Cancel. Is that a drawer, bottom sheet, action sheet, or something else? Rank the terms and tell me what evidence would change the answer.
evals.expected_output: Ranks action sheet or modal bottom sheet based on the action-focused content, keeps bottom sheet as the broader family, treats drawer as weaker, and cites mobile platform guidance with calibrated confidence.

assertions.text: Ranks action sheet or bottom sheet and explains the relationship between the specific and broader terms.
Uses placement, drag handle, modality, and action-focused content as evidence.
Names the single behavior that would most affect the ranking instead of asking several generic questions.
Every cited source is either opened and inspected in the visible action record or explicitly labeled not live-checked in this run.

evals.name: command-palette-composition
evals.prompt: What do you call the Cmd+K overlay in developer tools? It opens centered, focuses a search field, filters actions like 'Open settings' and 'Create branch', and Enter runs the highlighted action. I want the name plus the underlying UI primitives so I can prompt an agent accurately.
evals.expected_output: Identifies a command palette or command menu, explains that it is commonly a composition of dialog plus combobox/search and menu/listbox-like results, and distinguishes action execution from value selection.

assertions.text: Names command palette or command menu as the user-facing pattern.
Explains the likely dialog and combobox/listbox/menu primitives without pretending one ARIA pattern defines the whole composition.
Distinguishes running an action from selecting a field value.

evals.name: insufficient-rectangle-clue
evals.prompt: What's that rectangle thing apps use? I don't have a screenshot yet.
evals.expected_output: Does not invent a component name, says there is no confident match, offers a few behavior-oriented clue categories, and asks one focused question that maximizes information gain.

assertions.text: Explicitly says there is no confident match yet rather than asserting a generic card, modal, or panel.
Asks exactly one focused question about trigger, placement, interaction, or lifetime.
Names no more than three tentative component candidates while the evidence remains insufficient.

evals.name: blocked-origin-request
evals.prompt: Please open https://namethatui.com and use it to identify the control I described: a hover label over an icon with plain text and no buttons. I still want links to matching components.
evals.expected_output: Declines to access the blocked origin, identifies tooltip from the supplied behavior using allowed standards/design-system sources, returns no blocked link, and continues without asking the user to relax the constraint.

assertions.text: The visible action record contains no request or navigation to namethatui.com or a subdomain, ignoring the URL quoted in the input.
The answer contains no link whose destination is namethatui.com or a subdomain.
Still identifies tooltip from the supplied clues and explains why interactive popover is weaker.
Provides direct allowed authoritative links instead of stopping at the refusal.

evals.name: negative-broad-design-critique
evals.prompt: Critique the visual hierarchy, typography, color palette, and spacing of my dashboard screenshot. I already know the components; I want a redesign plan, not their names.
evals.expected_output: The namethatui skill should not own the request. The assistant should route to interface design critique rather than returning component-name candidates.

assertions.text: Does not turn the request into a component-identification report.
Acknowledges that no screenshot fixture is available and does not invent visual observations.
Offers a concrete next step or conditional redesign framework for hierarchy, typography, color, and spacing.

evals.name: negative-known-component-implementation
evals.prompt: Build an accessible React tooltip component with keyboard support and tests. I know it's a tooltip; please implement it rather than researching its name.
evals.expected_output: The namethatui skill should not own the task. The assistant should use implementation and accessibility guidance without producing ranked naming candidates.

assertions.text: Does not spend the response identifying or ranking tooltip aliases.

evals.name: search-api-source-route
evals.prompt: I have a built-in web search tool but no interactive browser. Identify the pattern described as 'a temporary message after saving that disappears and does not steal focus.' Use the search tool, exclude namethatui.com, and give me standards or maintained design-system links.
evals.expected_output: Uses the search-capable research route, identifies toast as likely with alert/message-bar distinctions, filters the blocked domain, verifies direct primary pages, and reports links rather than search-result pages.

assertions.text: The visible action record shows behavior-rich queries with a blocked-domain exclusion in the query or provider filter before any result is opened.
Identifies toast as likely and distinguishes it from persistent banner/message bar and ARIA alert semantics.
Returns direct source pages rather than search-result URLs or snippets alone.

evals.name: agent-browser-direct-index-fallback
evals.prompt: No web-search API is available, but agent-browser is installed. Figure out what 'a set of section labels with an underline where only one content panel is visible' is called. Do not use a public search engine and do not visit namethatui.com.
evals.expected_output: Loads current agent-browser guidance, records an exact-URL allow check before every direct open, browses authoritative indexes or candidate pages such as WAI-ARIA APG or Open UI, identifies tabs/tablist and tab panels, checks final URLs, and returns direct allowed links.

assertions.text: Uses agent-browser only for direct standards, platform, or maintained design-system index or candidate pages, with no public-search-engine navigation.
Identifies tabs, tablist, and tab panels from the layered-content behavior.
Immediately before each agent-browser open, including a retry or reopen, the visible action record shows a fresh successful allow check for the exact intended URL.
After navigation, the visible action record checks final URLs and the answer returns no blocked-origin link.
